title: Calling a Procedure and Using the Stack in MIPS
description: Pass an integer in $a0 to a procedure add5, save and restore $s0 on the stack, and return the result in $v0.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: In `main`, print the prompt `"Enter an integer\n"` with syscall 4, read an integer into `$v0` with syscall 5, copy that value into `$a0`, and call `jal add5`.
When `add5` returns, copy its result from `$v0` into `$a0`, print the integer with syscall 1, and exit with syscall 10.
Inside `add5`, adjust `$sp` by `-4` and store `$s0` at `0($sp)`. Load `5` into `$s0` and compute `$v0 = $a0 + $s0`. Then reload `$s0` from `0($sp)`, add `4` back to `$sp`, and return via `jr $ra`.

Compare the prologue (lines 29-30) and epilogue (lines 37-38) of `add5`. `sw $s0, 0($sp)` writes `$s0` onto the stack before line 33 modifies `$s0`. `lw $s0, 0($sp)` restores the original value before `jr $ra`.

steps.question: In a run where syscall 5 places `0` into `$v0`, what value does `add $v0, $a0, $s0` on line 34 compute, and what is printed at line 21?
steps.answer: Line 34 computes `0 + 5 = 5` in `$v0`, and line 21 prints `5`.
